title: Let go, ii
logline: Tuesday. The week's orders. A stranger's diploma. A kid's drawing (a father; the same one? the strip won't say). Wood cuts them all the way he'd cut them in 2001. Nobody frames anything they'd have brought in 2001.

panels.composition: The counter. A CUSTOMER with a diploma. WOOD taking it.

image.prompt: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flat color, a customer handing a diploma across a frame-shop counter to a thin man

panels.composition: A FATHER in a mill jacket. A crayon drawing. He sets it down and steps back and says nothing. Wood looks at him one beat longer than the job needs.

image.prompt: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flat color, a man in a faded mill jacket setting a child's crayon drawing on a counter and stepping back in silence, a thin man looking at him a beat too long, no words
image.notes: Rhymes with dw_2001-02-05. Whether it's the same man is reserved.

panels.composition: Wood cutting the mat for the drawing. Red frame. No mat, actually — he takes the mat back out. The kids' rule.

image.prompt: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flat color, close-up of a thin man's hands setting aside a cut mat and fitting a child's drawing into a red frame with no mat

panels.composition: The father taking it. One nod. Gone. The Owner, from the back, watching Wood watch the door.

image.prompt: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flat color, a thin man watching a frame-shop door close while an older woman at the back watches him, no words

art.line: brush-pen; the flats cleaner; the Sundays the point now

notes: The father in the mill jacket, again or not. Red frame, no mat.
